name: Jayaswal Neco Industries Ltd
tagline: Integrated Nagpur-Chhattisgarh steel/pig-iron/casting group in a genuine deleveraging turnaround — four straight strong quarters, secured debt down 22% in FY26, interest cost refinanced from ~17.5% to 12.5% via Tata Capital — but ~55% of promoter equity re-pledged to the NCD debenture trustee and an unrelated sister-company defence-export controversy remain overhangs
business_overview: JNIL (flagship of the Neco Group, promoted by Basant Lall Shaw and the Jayaswal family) makes billets, rolled products, pig iron & skull, sponge iron, pellets, steel and iron & steel castings from an integrated Siltara (Raipur, Chhattisgarh) facility with captive iron-ore mining (~3 MnTPA operating vs 4 MnTPA approved, 6 MnTPA EC secured) and captive power. Also has a rolling-mill business serving auto customers, currently running at low utilisation. Referred to NCLT in 2018 by a bank consortium; restructuring effective May 2022; high-cost debt refinanced by Tata Capital (Rs 2,300 Cr at 12.5% vs prior ~17.5%), completed Dec 2025.
fundamentals_table: Trailing ROE ~9%, ROCE ~15% and improving as FY26 PAT (Rs 463 Cr) lands; historical returns depressed by restructuring years
FY26 secured debt Rs 2,118 Cr (down 22% YoY); total borrowings ~Rs 4,100 Cr; structure now ~Rs 1,800 Cr NCD + ~Rs 500 Cr WC; scheduled repayments Rs 383 Cr in FY27 coverable from operating cash flow

Dec-2025: prior 55.10% pledge released after refinance; immediately a FRESH pledge on ~53.48 Cr shares (~55% of equity) created in favour of Vistra ITCL as NCD debenture trustee — structural collateral with a repayment-linked release, not a margin/distress pledge, but ~99% of promoter holding is encumbered
FY26 Rs 7,132 Cr (+19% YoY); Q1 FY27 Rs 2,107 Cr (+28% YoY)
FY26 Rs 1,341 Cr (+41% YoY); Q1 FY27 Rs 396 Cr (+26% YoY), margin ~18.8%
FY26 Rs 463 Cr (+311% vs Rs 113 Cr FY25); Q4 FY26 Rs 191 Cr; Q1 FY27 Rs 194 Cr (+108% YoY); TTM PAT ~Rs 560 Cr → P/E ~15x
~Rs 400 Cr FY26 → guided ~Rs 288 Cr FY27 on Tata Capital refinance (rate 17.5% → 12.5%)
fundamentals_narrative: The turnaround is no longer a single quarter: Q1 FY26 swung loss-to-profit (Rs 93 Cr vs -Rs 32 Cr), Q4 FY26 PAT was Rs 191 Cr and Q1 FY27 Rs 194 Cr (+108% YoY on +28% revenue), with EBITDA margin holding ~19%. FY26 delivered Rs 7,132 Cr revenue (+19%), Rs 1,341 Cr EBITDA (+41%) and Rs 463 Cr PAT (+311%). Two structural drivers: (1) deleveraging — secured debt cut 22% to Rs 2,118 Cr in FY26 and the residual high-cost debt refinanced by Tata Capital at 12.5% (from ~17.5%), guided to lower interest cost from ~Rs 400 Cr to ~Rs 288 Cr in FY27; (2) captive iron-ore self-sufficiency (entire steel-plant ore requirement sourced internally) with a 6 MnTPA mine EC secured and a 1.5 MnTPA, Rs 720 Cr straight-grate pellet plant approved on a 24-month build, part-funded by a Rs 200 Cr promoter-group warrant issue (Vibrant Enterprises, Rs 89.13/warrant). Caveats: commodity-steel cyclicality against still-material leverage, ~99% of promoter holding pledged (to the NCD debenture trustee), persistently low rolling-mill utilisation (pig iron sold in the open market rather than fed downstream), and the unrelated Neco Defence Munitions / Estonia arbitration reputational overhang on a sister entity.
technical_read: Thread's most recent post (Sept-2026) reads the stock as 'turning around after base building' with an 82-92 support zone, arguing the recent news-driven dip is unlikely to break that base absent actual business impact — not independently verified via TradingView this pass.

bse_notes: 6-mo announcements: FY26 results + Rs 200 Cr warrant issue approved (EGM May 2026); 1.5 MnTPA pellet plant (Rs 720 Cr, 24-mo) board-approved; Tata Capital Rs 2,300 Cr refinance completed Dec 2025; Dec-2025 promoter pledge release followed by fresh Vistra ITCL debenture-trustee pledge on ~55% of equity; company clarification distancing itself from Neco Defence Munitions / Estonia dispute (Sep 2026).
bull_case: Four consecutive strong quarters, not one: Q1 FY26 Rs 93 Cr PAT (loss-to-profit) -> Q4 FY26 Rs 191 Cr -> Q1 FY27 Rs 194 Cr (+108% YoY on +28% revenue), EBITDA margin holding ~19%

Deleveraging is executing: FY26 secured debt down 22% to Rs 2,118 Cr; Tata Capital refinanced the residual high-cost debt at 12.5% (from ~17.5%), cutting guided interest cost from ~Rs 400 Cr (FY26) to ~Rs 288 Cr (FY27) — a mechanical PAT tailwind independent of steel prices

Captive iron ore covers the entire steel-plant requirement; 6 MnTPA mine EC secured and a 1.5 MnTPA / Rs 720 Cr pellet plant approved (24-mo build), part-funded by a Rs 200 Cr promoter-group warrant issue at Rs 89.13 — promoters adding equity, holding rising 55.15% -> ~56%
TTM P/E ~15x and ~12-13x on a plausible FY27 (interest saving + volume) is undemanding for a deleveraging integrated producer
bear_case: Commodity-steel cyclicality against still-material leverage (~Rs 4,100 Cr total borrowings, Rs 2,118 Cr secured) — the earnings run-rate has to hold through a steel-price down-cycle, not just this one

~99% of promoter holding is pledged: the Dec-2025 release was immediately followed by a fresh pledge on ~53.48 Cr shares (~55% of equity) to Vistra ITCL as NCD debenture trustee. Structural refinancing collateral with a repayment-linked release, not distress selling — but the 'clean 0% pledge' read in earlier notes is outdated

Rolling-mill utilisation persistently low — pig iron is sold in the open market rather than feeding downstream capacity, a product-mix / execution gap a trusted user (richbandit) raised and management has not clearly addressed publicly

Reputational overhang: Neco Defence Munitions (a sister company, not a JNIL subsidiary) is central to a ~EUR70m Estonian ammunition-supply dispute now in international arbitration; JNIL has issued a clarification distancing itself, but the cross-group read-through is an unresolved monitor item (does not meet this screen's formal red-flag criteria)
No live-theme match in active_themes.json — a plain commodity-steel + deleveraging discovery candidate, not a thematic tailwind play
verdict_headline: A genuine deleveraging + earnings turnaround now four quarters deep, with a refinance that mechanically lifts FY27 PAT — kept at Medium given commodity cyclicality, still-material leverage, ~99% promoter pledge to the NCD trustee, and an unresolved sister-company reputational overhang
verdict_reasoning: No live-theme match — recency/discovery candidate (discover.py), not a thematic hit

Trailing-average-vs-live-inflection rule applied: weak multi-year ROE/leverage profile but a sustained recent inflection (four strong quarters, loss-to-profit YoY, EBITDA margin ~19%) plus two structural drivers — a completed Tata Capital refinance (17.5% -> 12.5%) that cuts guided interest ~Rs 400 Cr -> ~Rs 288 Cr in FY27, and an approved 6 MnTPA iron-ore EC + 1.5 MnTPA pellet plant — permits a 10x label at capped conviction with an 'unconfirmed' caveat
Four-box score 3.0 (tailwind yes on the live deleveraging inflection, valuation yes at ~15x TTM / ~12-13x forward; tam/moat weak) independently clears the 10x bar

Conviction capped at Medium: (a) commodity-steel cyclicality against still-material leverage (~Rs 4,100 Cr total borrowings), (b) ~99% of promoter holding pledged to the NCD debenture trustee (structural, repayment-linked release — but the earlier 'clean 0% pledge' framing is outdated), (c) unresolved rolling-mill-utilisation execution question raised by a trusted user, and (d) the Neco Defence Munitions / Estonia arbitration overhang on a sister entity — treated as a caution flag, not a formal red flag, since it does not implicate JNIL itself under the AVOID/EXCLUDE criteria

track_record.note: FY24-FY26 verifiable from current filings. FY24: loss. FY25: PAT Rs 113 Cr, ROCE well below 15%. FY26: revenue +19% and ROCE ~15% as PAT jumped to Rs 463 Cr — the only year clearing both the >=10% revenue-growth and >=15% ROCE bars. Multi-year record is depressed by the 2018 NCLT reference and 2022 restructuring; the investable window is the FY26-onward turnaround, not the history.

four_box.note: Tailwind yes (small/mid-cap live-inflection carve-out): a real, sustained recent inflection — four strong quarters, a completed Tata Capital refinance mechanically cutting FY27 interest ~Rs 400 Cr -> ~Rs 288 Cr, secured debt -22% in FY26, plus an approved 6 MnTPA iron-ore EC and 1.5 MnTPA pellet plant. TAM weak: domestic long/alloy steel + castings is large but commoditised and cyclical, no differentiated demand driver. Moat weak: captive iron ore + backward integration is a genuine cost advantage but the business is still a price-taker. Valuation yes: ~Rs 8,700 Cr cap on ~Rs 560 Cr TTM PAT (~15x) and ~12-13x on a plausible FY27 is undemanding for a deleveraging integrated producer. Score 3.0 -> 10x-in-2-3-years permitted; conviction held at Medium on cyclicality + leverage + ~99% promoter pledge to the NCD trustee + sister-company overhang.
